topic: How corporate incentives systematically erode your personal sense of agency
angle: While autonomy support and work autonomy are linked to positive outcomes, algorithmic management creates a recursive cycle where worker resistance can be co-opted by platforms to further compress agency.
title: The Erosion of Personal Agency

hooks.text: Is your work autonomy an illusion?
You seek flexibility but find algorithmic control.
You are training the system that manages you.
A glowing screen in a quiet office.

reveal.headline: Your resistance to algorithmic management may reinforce your own control.
reveal.body: Workers who try to resist algorithmic management may inadvertently contribute to their own control. This happens through recursive dynamics that compress worker agency. The evidence on this is mixed and still developing.

explain.headline: Platforms absorb your efforts to gain autonomy.
explain.body: Algorithmic management creates a tension between promised flexibility and actual control. While autonomy support is linked to well-being, these systems can systematically absorb worker efforts to gain agency.

matters.headline: Your agency may be a feedback loop.
matters.body: That may be why your attempts to work smarter or push back against the system end up refining the very tools that manage you.

example.headline: A notification on your phone.
example.body: You adjust your pace to hit a metric. You think you are optimizing your day. The system records the change and adjusts your next task accordingly.

question.headline: Who is actually making your choices today?

verdict: The evidence shows that while autonomy is a key driver of well-being, algorithmic systems can create complex dynamics where worker efforts to gain agency are systematically absorbed by the platform.
caveat: The research on algorithmic management is still developing, with some studies highlighting a gap in global and comparative analysis.
caption:
Corporate systems are reshaping how you experience personal agency.

Research shows that algorithmic management creates a tension between flexibility and control. Some evidence suggests that worker resistance can be co-opted by platforms, though research in this area is still developing and lacks global analysis.
